description: Spring Boot plugin adding explicit, AI-friendly YAML endpoint orchestration to Spring Boot REST so each endpoint's flow is declared and generatable from one readable file.
rules: OfficeFloor is a progressive Spring Boot add-on, not a replacement. Add the officefloor-rest-spring-boot-starter dependency and keep existing Spring beans, security, persistence and actuator config intact.

A REST endpoint is a YAML file under src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/. The file name encodes method and path as {path}.{METHOD}.yml (greeting.GET.yml maps to GET /greeting). Directory nesting becomes path segments; index.{METHOD}.yml maps to /.
Curly-brace segments in a file or directory name become URL path variables, e.g. officefloor/rest/greeting/{name}.GET.yml maps to GET /greeting/{name}.

Inside a YAML endpoint file each top-level entry is a developer-named step (the label is not a keyword) that declares a handler via `class:`. The first entry in the file is the entry point invoked when the request arrives.
If a handler class has a single public method it is used automatically; if it has more than one public method the step must specify `method:` to name which one to call, or start-up fails.

Chain steps with `next: <step>` for an unconditional next step, or with an `outputs:` map (named branch to step) for conditional flow. This YAML file is the complete, readable specification of the endpoint's steps, order and branches.

In code: a `next:` step passes data by returning a value, received as an @Parameter. An `outputs:` branch is a custom @FunctionalInterface parameter annotated @Flow("name"); calling its method routes to the mapped step and passes its argument on.

Exceptions (escalations) use the same model as flows: a step throws a checked exception (must extend Exception, so it is in the throws clause) and the handler receives it as an @Parameter, responding via ObjectResponse. No Spring annotations needed.

Route escalations at three levels, highest precedence first: an `escalations:` map on a step, a `composition:` block for the file, or a global officefloor/escalation/<exception-FQCN>.yml file. Unmatched exceptions fall through to Spring @ControllerAdvice.

Wrap a step in cross-cutting concerns with `govern: [ ... ]`, e.g. `govern: [ transaction ]` or `govern: [ audit ]`. Governance is defined under officefloor/govern/, and its failures route through the same escalation mechanism.

Handler classes are plain Java, no @RestController or @RequestMapping. A method parameter whose type matches a Spring bean is injected by type; standard Spring MVC annotations (@PathVariable, @RequestParam, @RequestBody, ...) are also supported.

Always use the name= attribute form on Spring parameter annotations, e.g. @PathVariable(name = "name"). The shorthand @PathVariable("name") relies on @AliasFor synthesis that OfficeFloor does not apply, so it silently binds an empty value.
Write the JSON response with ObjectResponse<T> (response.send(obj)); use ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>> when you need custom headers or a non-200 status. No @ResponseBody is required.

Two version-specific starters exist: officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter (Spring Boot 3.x) and officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter (Spring Boot 4.x). Add only the one matching your generation; mixing versions causes runtime binary incompatibilities.

Prefer defining, generating and refactoring endpoints from the YAML file, since it makes the whole endpoint structure explicit in one place rather than implicit across annotations and Spring's call stack.
